metadata.title: You're Just a Text File
metadata.purpose: Show viewers how to compress 20 years of voice and taste into a portable about-me.md file using a 100-question self-interview with Claude, then make it work across any AI tool.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro) — durations are word-count estimates until GATE 0 audio lock

props.command: What is: You're Just a Text File?

beats.narration_text: Aloha. This is Liam, in for Bear. What if Claude could write in your exact voice — not a close approximation, but you? One text file. Two hours. Any AI becomes you.

props.answer_preview: Claude sounds exactly like you — because it read your about-me file first.
props.command: What if Claude could write in your exact voice — not a close approximation, but you?

beats.narration_text: You're just a text file. That feels reductive. It's not. Your voice — the phrase your oldest friend imitates, the analogy you've written three times this year without noticing — those are patterns. Patterns fit in a file.

card.sub: Your voice is a set of patterns. Patterns fit in a text file. One file, and any AI becomes you.

beats.narration_text: The process: open Claude with Extended Thinking on. Run one prompt — a hundred-question self-interview. Answer everything. Dictate your answers with a voice-to-text tool like Wispr Flow; it's faster and more honest. You'll end up with a massive self-interview. That's the raw material.

illustration.concept: Three-step process: 1. 100-question interview prompt → 2. ~20,000-word raw dump → 3. compress to about-me.md
illustration.layout: Horizontal flow, left to right. Step 1: prompt icon + '100 questions'. Arrow. Step 2: large text block icon + '~20,000 words'. Arrow. Step 3: clean file icon + 'about-me.md'. Labels below each step.

beats.narration_text: Don't stop at the raw dump. Most people do. That file is too big — it eats your context window and costs you tokens on every turn. In the same conversation, run a second prompt: compress this into an efficient about-me file. Claude distills it. You get a tight, portable file that any AI can load cheaply.

card.sub: The raw interview is too big. A second prompt compresses it into a tight about-me.md that fits any context window.

beats.narration_text: You'll resist this. Every time, for four reasons. One: it feels reductive. It doesn't make you smaller — it makes you compatible with AI. Two: it feels scary. When you read yourself in one file, there's nowhere left to hide. Three: you think self-knowledge takes decades. This forces you to articulate what you already know. Four: you've built an identity on being hard to capture. That mystery, when you look at it closely, is usually just being vague.

illustration.concept: Four resistance reasons displayed as a 2x2 grid with objection + reframe pairs
illustration.layout: 2×2 grid. Each cell: objection in italic + reframe in normal weight beneath. Cells reveal in reading order (left-right, top-bottom), 0.4 s each.

beats.narration_text: What you get on the other side. The file is portable — it works in Claude, in other AI tools, anywhere. You can give it to a teammate so they draft in your voice when you're offline. You stop re-deciding how you write every Monday. You do the hard work once, and then ship.

card.sub: Your about-me file works in any AI tool. Give it to your team. Stop re-deciding your voice every Monday.

beats.narration_text: Edit it often. You change. Your taste changes. That's called life. Every time you find something Claude did that felt wrong, go to Obsidian, open about-me.md, and add one line: 'Never do X.' Or 'Replace Y with Z always.' The file is alive. Keep it that way.

card.sub: Every time Claude gets something wrong, fix it in about-me.md. One line. The file learns as you change.

beats.narration_text: Setup: Claude with Extended Thinking. Use Wispr Flow — free, turns your voice into text — to answer the hundred questions faster and more honestly. Use Obsidian to edit the compressed file afterward. Three tools. Two hours. One file that works forever.

card.sub: Claude + Extended Thinking for the interview. Wispr Flow for voice dictation. Obsidian to edit afterward.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Block two hours this week. Open a fresh Claude chat with Extended Thinking on. Run the hundred-question interview. Answer out loud with Wispr Flow. Compress it. Upload the file to your Cowork folder. Run one writing task and compare the before and after.

card.sub: 100-question interview → compress → upload to Cowork. Run one writing task. Compare before and after.

beats.narration_text: You are not just a text file. But you fit in one. This is Liam, in for Bear.

card.sub: this is Liam, in for Bear

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: you want Claude to write in your voice across all your work — not just one task. Ask Claude to show you the voice file approach: how to build a text file that captures your tone, register, and style patterns, how to include it in a prompt without inflating the context, and how to update it when your voice evolves.

props.command: I want Claude to write in my voice across all my work — not just one task.
